pr.title: Save 2 pointers in `TerminatorKind` (96 → 80 bytes)
pr.description:
These things don't need to be `Vec`s; boxed slices are enough.

The frequent one here is call arguments, but MIR building knows the number of arguments from the THIR, so the collect is always getting the allocation right in the first place, and thus this shouldn't ever add the shrink-in-place overhead.
pr.author: scottmcm

processing.reason: PR #126784 is a pure MIR representation/ownership refactor: `TerminatorKind::Call::args`, inline-asm `operands`, and `targets` change from `Vec<T>` to `Box<[T]>`, with consumers adjusted to exact-arity extraction (`take_array`, `Box::try_from`) instead of `pop`/`drain`/`mem::take`. There is no historically incorrect value transformation to encode. The only behavioral differences are on malformed MIR arity (e.g. old `pop()` accepting extra/missing args where exact destructuring rejects them); such malformed MIR cannot be produced by ordinary Rust source inputs, and manufacturing a custom-MIR arity mismatch would test an unreachable compiler invariant rather than the PR's semantics. On all well-formed calls and inline asm, the old and new implementations produce identical program values, as the frozen analysis itself concludes. Therefore no source-grounded original/transformed function pair can validly demonstrate a semantic miscompile.

analysis.summary: MIR terminator payloads were converted from growable `Vec`s to boxed slices to shrink `TerminatorKind` from 96 to 80 bytes. The reusable correctness point is that every producer and consumer must preserve exact call/inline-asm arity while switching from `Vec` mutation (`pop`, `drain`, `mem::take`) to consuming boxed-slice destructuring such as `take_array`.
analysis.originalLogic: `TerminatorKind::Call` stored `args: Vec<Spanned<Operand<'tcx>>>`, and inline asm stored `operands: Vec<InlineAsmOperand<'tcx>>` plus `targets: Vec<BasicBlock>`. Consumers used growable-vector operations: `InstSimplify` acquired the last operand with `args.pop().unwrap()`, `LowerIntrinsics` used `args.drain(..)`/`next()` or `std::mem::take(args)` conversions, `StateTransform` popped the last argument, and `Inline` accepted/produced `Vec`s for call arguments. Size assertions encoded the larger layout, including `static_assert_size!(TerminatorKind<'_>, 96);`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: No semantic miscompile is evidenced. The historical implementation is the pre-optimization representation: growable `Vec`s for terminator call arguments and inline-assembly operands/targets, with consumers mutating or borrowing those vectors. The optimization replaces them with `Box<[T]>` and updates consumers to consume/destructure the boxed slices; it is a layout/ownership change, not a historical incorrect rewrite of program semantics.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR bodies containing `TerminatorKind::Call` and `TerminatorKind::InlineAsm`, produced from ordinary Rust calls and method calls, closure calls using the `RustCall` ABI, box allocation calls, drop-glue destructor calls, shims, intrinsic calls lowered by `LowerIntrinsics`, async/coroutine `get_context` calls, and test mock bodies. Relevant intrinsic inputs include `copy_nonoverlapping`, `assume`, wrapping/unchecked arithmetic, overflow intrinsics, `read_via_copy`, `write_via_move`, `offset`, `transmute`/`transmute_unchecked`, `aggregate_raw_ptr`, `ptr_metadata`, and `const_eval_select`.
analysis.trigger: Any refactoring or optimization that changes `TerminatorKind` array fields from `Vec` to `Box<[T]>`, or any pass that reads, replaces, or mutates call arguments or inline-assembly operands/targets. The compact representation depends on producers already knowing the exact element count, especially call arguments built from THIR.
preconditions: All construction sites must produce `Box<[T]>` rather than `Vec<T>`; e.g. `[].into()`, `vec![...]` replaced by array `.into()`, or `targets.into_boxed_slice()`.
Consumers that need owned elements must use exact-arity extraction such as `take_array(args)` or `Box::try_from(args)`, because a boxed slice cannot be `pop`ped or `drain`ed like a `Vec`.

The arity of each intrinsic/call form is an internal MIR invariant; malformed arity must be handled explicitly with `bug!`, `span_bug!`, `unreachable!()`, or an early return rather than accidentally indexing.
Generic MIR folding over these fields requires a `TypeFoldable` implementation for `Box<[T]>`, here by converting to `Vec`, folding, and converting back to a boxed slice.
Iteration over an owned `Box<[T]>` must consume it correctly; this patch used `<_>::into_iter(args)` with an edition-2024 FIXME.
pitfalls: `Vec::pop()` and `drain(..).next()` have different acceptance behavior from exact destructuring: old `InstSimplify` took the last argument and `StateTransform` popped one, whereas exact boxed-slice extraction requires exactly one argument.
`args.as_slice()` only borrows; replacing it with `take_array(args)` consumes/empties the field, so later use of `args` changes.

Converting a right-sized `Vec` via `into_boxed_slice()` can trigger shrink-in-place work; direct collection into a boxed slice is preferable when the count is already known. The PR states the common call-argument path should not add this overhead because THIR supplies the argument count.
Arity-mismatch diagnostics differ by pass: `LowerIntrinsics` uses `bug!`/`span_bug!`, `InstSimplify` returns without simplifying, and `const_eval_select` remapping uses `unreachable!()`.
Updating only the field type is insufficient: all producers, consumers, test mock bodies, and type-folding support must be updated together.
Size assertions must be adjusted for the container layout change as well as `TerminatorKind` itself: the patch changes `Terminator` 112 to 96 and `BasicBlockData` 144 to 128.
analysis.testStrategy: Construct MIR/unit inputs that contain calls and inline assembly, then exercise each touched pass. Cover normal calls, closure `RustCall` inlining, empty-argument calls, one- and multi-argument intrinsics, intrinsic arity mismatch behavior, inline asm with targets/unwind, and async coroutine `get_context` elimination. Assert the representation invariants with `static_assert_size!` for `TerminatorKind`, `Terminator`, and `BasicBlockData`. Include unit tests that build `TerminatorKind::Call` directly with boxed slices and tests that fold MIR containing boxed-slice fields. Since the historical patch only updates existing test helper constructions and adds no regression test file, focus tests on the representation conversion and exact-arity consumer behavior. No compiler was built and no execution or bug reproduction is claimed.
